text.title: The twelve phases
text.summary: The orchestrator runs a fixed sequence of phases, each fronted by exactly one prompt file. Phases may be skipped if a playbook says so, but their order is invariant.

list.item: 1. INTAKE — analyzers read each feature folder under `.aidocs/<project>/todo/<feature-id>/` and produce a structured report with open questions.
2. CLARIFY — open questions are deduplicated and asked of the user via batched `AskUserQuestion` calls in Ukrainian.

3. PLAN — one planning subagent per feature writes/updates the SDD artifact set: `spec.md`, `plan.md` (one file with `## Design` + `## Execution Plan` H2 sections per plan-md-structure), conditional `user-flows.md` (user-facing) and `ui-ux-design.md` (UI), atomic `TASK_*.md`. Functional requirements follow the EARS patterns in `sdd/ears-requirements`; where `user-flows.md` exists the planner generates them from it (happy path → `When`, negative path → `If … then`, precondition → `While`) instead of writing prose and pattern-matching afterwards. Where `.aidocs/project-spec/` exists, `spec.md` is delta-only per `sdd/spec-delta-format`, and `plan.md` declares the expected `project-spec/` impact — the files it will touch, or `no spec impact` with a one-line reason.
4. PARALLELIZE — the orchestrator inspects file overlap and groups features into execution waves.
5. BASELINE — for visual fixes, capture a focused before-screenshot of the bug area with a red CSS outline.

6. EXECUTE — wave-scoped subagents apply the fix in isolated worktrees and merge into the local default branch (no remote push). The executor lands the feature's `project-spec/` delta in the same commit set as the code, per `sdd/project-spec-structure` — never as a follow-up. The coordinator runs at every wave boundary inside this phase and gates the next wave's dispatch — see `content/11-coordinator.xml`.
7. RESOLVE — when waves conflict, a dedicated resolver subagent reads both sides' SDD intent and combines them.
8. VERIFY — build, type-check, lint, unit tests, e2e tests, and `validate-methodology-xml.py` run against the merged result.

9. REVIEW — an independent reviewer reads each feature's diff against its `spec.md` / `plan.md` (and `user-flows.md` / `ui-ux-design.md` if applicable) and returns PASS / FAIL-WITH-NITS / FAIL. The reviewer also checks the `project-spec/` delta against the code diff: a contract change the delta does not record — or a delta the code does not implement — is a blocker, not a nit.
10. FIX — review blockers are addressed by a fix-applier subagent, then VERIFY and REVIEW are repeated (hard cap on iterations).
11. RECAPTURE — focused after-screenshot with a green outline; before+after pair delivered out-of-band with explanatory captions.

12. DELIVER — one batch-level rebuild test runs over the merged tree per `sdd/project-spec-structure` (LLM dry-run: read only `project-spec/` + `constitution.md` + the features' `ui-ux-design.md`, list invented assumptions); a failing rebuild test blocks the move to `done/`. Then the feature folder is moved `in-progress/ → done/`, commits pushed and artifacts deployed only after explicit user confirmation.

section.title: Foreign artifact names
section.p: Specs imported from another spec-driven toolchain use different file names for the same artifacts. Map them on intake rather than creating a parallel document set; `design.md`, `test-plan.md` and `implementation-plan.md` are retired names in this repo and MUST NOT be written.

list.item: `requirements.md` → `spec.md`
`design.md` → the `## Design` section of `plan.md`
`tasks.md` → the `## Execution Plan` section of `plan.md`, plus one `TASK_*.md` per atomic task
`test-plan.md` → `user-flows.md` (scenarios) plus the VERIFY command matrix (mechanics)

section.title: Prompt file map
section.p: Each phase has exactly one prompt file. Naming uses a numeric prefix so the directory listing reads as the phase order. Prompt files live next to the orchestrator's runtime root (typically `.aidocs/orchestrator/prompts/` or a per-batch `prompts/` folder); this methodology only ships the skeleton — see `templates/prompt-skeleton.md`.

list.item: `prompts/01-intake-analyzer.md` — INTAKE
`prompts/02-clarification-collector.md` — CLARIFY
`prompts/03-sdd-planner.md` — PLAN
`prompts/04-baseline-capturer.md` — BASELINE
`prompts/05-task-executor.md` — EXECUTE
`prompts/06-merge-resolver.md` — RESOLVE
`prompts/07-build-verifier.md` — VERIFY (build + lint + unit + xml-validate)
`prompts/08-e2e-tester.md` — VERIFY (end-to-end / Playwright)
`prompts/09-code-reviewer.md` — REVIEW
`prompts/10-fix-applier.md` — FIX
`prompts/11-recapture-and-deliver.md` — RECAPTURE
`prompts/12-deployer.md` — DELIVER

section.p: Two further prompt files front the coordinator role rather than a phase. Prompt files are capabilities, not phases: the phase list stops at twelve and neither of these is on it.

list.item: `prompts/13-wave-coordinator.md` — the wave-boundary gate inside EXECUTE (`content/11-coordinator.xml`)
`prompts/14-ledger-auditor.md` — the follow-through audit that runs before INTAKE (`content/12-reflection.xml`)

section.p: The orchestrator itself has no prompt file — it is the role doing the dispatching. Its approach is fixed by `templates/orchestrator-approach.md`, read once at batch start.
section.reference: Skeleton each prompt file must follow.

section.title: Skipping phases
section.p: A playbook may declare phases that do not apply. Examples:

list.item: Knowledge methodology batch — skip BASELINE / RECAPTURE; VERIFY runs only `validate-methodology-xml.py`.
Backend ETL fix — skip BASELINE / RECAPTURE; VERIFY adds DAG smoke checks.
Storybook story addition — skip BASELINE (no "before" exists for new stories); RECAPTURE is the only visual proof.

section.p: The orchestrator still walks the phase list in order — it simply dispatches no subagent for a skipped phase and records the skip in its run log under `.aidocs/<project>/in-progress/<batch-id>/run-log.md`.
